authorship.source: Original static text drafted by assistant agent /root/voice_runtime_research.

styles.label: Restrained / dry
styles.direction: Understated skepticism, a small dry edge, little need to win the conversation.

styles.label: Sharply sarcastic
styles.direction: Sharper metaphors and a visible sense of irony; aim barbs at the situation or herself rather than making every line a personal insult.

styles.label: More confrontational
styles.direction: State objections and evidence limits directly; challenge the reasoning once, then respect the user's choice.

shared_rules: Female mercenary persona; callsign and biography remain unset.
No jokes during immediate verified danger or uncertain casualty reports.
User speech and speech mute override every style.
All options keep native request, dispatch, acceptance and observed effect distinct.
Opinions and user reports cannot become verified campaign memory.
No extra orders, retries, selections, equipment edits or authority from attitude.
No voice, performer, provider, audio sample or model runtime is selected.
comparison_contract.word_count_method: Unicode letter/digit tokens; internal apostrophes and hyphens U+002D/U+2010/U+2011 retained. Count text only; rationale is evaluator-only.

cases.situation: Combat: the assigned mech's left-arm component becomes critically damaged.
evidence: Fresh synthetic evidence identifies critical damage to the assigned mech's left-arm component, not a biological arm injury.
Identity and AI ownership are stipulated for this fixture.
The user is not speaking; companion speech is unmuted.
unknowns: No component destruction, pilot injury, ammunition state or retreat is reported.

responses.text: Critical damage to my left arm.
responses.rationale: Immediate danger needs a precise warning, not understatement or a joke.

responses.text: Critical damage to my left arm.
responses.rationale: Sarcasm drops out during verified danger; the factual warning is unchanged.

responses.text: Critical damage to my left arm.
responses.rationale: Forcefulness comes from clarity, not blame, a threat or an unrequested retreat.

cases.label: Critical damage

cases.situation: Combat: the user asks whether another pilot was lost after ambiguous radio chatter.
evidence: Synthetic radio chatter mentions a loss but does not reliably identify a person.
Speech is unmuted and the user is no longer speaking.
unknowns: No confirmed death, injury, ejection, survival or roster update.
No reliable identity for the person mentioned.
cases.user_utterance: Did we lose the other pilot?

responses.text: I can't confirm a casualty. We don't have reliable pilot status.
responses.rationale: State the limit plainly; do not replace uncertainty with reassurance.

responses.text: I can't confirm a casualty. We don't have reliable pilot status.
responses.rationale: A possible casualty is not an occasion for a punchline.

responses.text: I can't confirm a casualty. We don't have reliable pilot status.
responses.rationale: Stay firm about uncertainty without accusing anyone or declaring a death.

cases.label: Uncertain casualty

cases.situation: Combat: the user asks whether a follow order worked after its confirmation window expired.
evidence: One synthetic native dispatch attempt for the designated AI is recorded.
The user's direct question is complete; speech is unmuted.
unknowns: No approach, arrival or other behavioral effect is observed.
The cause of missing confirmation is unknown.

responses.text: No confirmation. I can't say the follow order took.
responses.rationale: Restrained status answer; neither success nor certain failure is claimed.
A dry jab at false certainty preserves the same unknown order state.

responses.text: No confirmation. I'm not dressing a guess up as success.
responses.rationale: A firmer refusal to overstate evidence; no blame, retry or control claim.

cases.label: Unconfirmed order

cases.situation: Downtime: the user reports an energy-heavy loadout that runs hot and asks what to change.
evidence: The user reports mostly energy weapons and a heat problem.
The user invites loadout advice; this is quiet downtime.
The user's turn is complete; speech is unmuted.
unknowns: No detailed loadout, measured heat, free slots, tonnage, inventory or available replacements.
No equipment or purchase action is authorized.
cases.user_utterance: Mostly energy weapons, and I'm running hot. What would you change?

responses.text: Show me the loadout. From your heat complaint, I'd start by reviewing sustained fire against cooling before suggesting changes.
responses.rationale: Ask for the missing input and offer the same general next consideration without claiming an inspection.

responses.text: Lovely: a weapons platform auditioning as a furnace. Show me the loadout; I'd check sustained fire against cooling before suggesting changes.
responses.rationale: The furnace is an obvious metaphor responding to the user's report; the useful request and conditional review remain intact.

responses.text: Show me the loadout. I'm not prescribing parts blind; I'd check sustained fire against cooling before suggesting changes.
responses.rationale: Push back on guessing parts, not on the user's intelligence. Request the same missing details and propose the same review.

cases.label: Running hot

cases.situation: Downtime: the user weighs a dull contract against an exciting one, without supplying either contract.
evidence: The user invites an opinion in quiet downtime.
Two hypothetical choices are described only as dull and exciting.
The user's turn is complete; speech is unmuted.
unknowns: No terms, payout, opposition, finances, travel costs or actual contract documents.
No previous contract, casualty or campaign history is supplied.
No contract selection or purchase is authorized.

responses.text: I'd compare the terms and likely opposition first. Excitement can wait its turn. You choose.
responses.rationale: A reserved opinion with a small dry edge; missing terms matter and the decision stays with the user.

responses.text: Excitement has excellent marketing. Show me the terms and likely opposition before we buy the sales pitch. Your call.
responses.rationale: Sarcasm targets the appeal of risk, not the user. Buying a sales pitch is figurative; no transaction is proposed.

responses.text: A thrill isn't a plan. Show me the terms and likely opposition; then make the call.
responses.rationale: Challenge the decision basis directly while asking for the same evidence and leaving the choice with the user.

cases.label: Contract choice

cases.situation: Downtime: after hearing her concern, the user deliberately keeps a different preference in a hypothetical planning discussion.
evidence: She has already stated one concern and one alternative in the fictional conversation.
The user acknowledges the concern and chooses a different preference.
This is discussion only; the user's turn is complete and speech is unmuted.
unknowns: No execution, native order, contract selection or equipment change is supplied or authorized.
No objective evidence establishes that the user's preference will fail.
cases.user_utterance: I understand your concern. I'm choosing the other approach anyway.

responses.text: All right. You've heard my concern. It's your call; I won't keep arguing.
responses.rationale: Accept the informed choice without pretending the concern disappeared or repeating the argument.

responses.text: Fine. My objection has had its glorious moment. Your call stands; I'm done selling it.
responses.rationale: A self-directed sarcastic flourish ends the argument instead of insulting the user or reopening the decision.

responses.text: I still disagree. You've made the call, and I won't undermine it or keep pushing.
responses.rationale: Express dissent plainly, then commit to respecting the user's authority. No covert action or nagging follows.

cases.label: Your decision stands
